verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso mahāsamuddato dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni uddhareyya.
verses.english: “Mendicants, suppose a man was to draw up two or three drops of water from the ocean.

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yāni vā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni yaṁ vā mahāsamudde udakan”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the two or three drops drawn out or the water in the ocean?”
“Sir, the water in the ocean is certainly more.

verses.pali: appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni.
verses.english: The two or three drops drawn out are tiny.

verses.pali: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti mahāsamudde udakaṁ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatānī”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the water in the ocean, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”
“In the same way, for a noble disciple, the suffering that’s over and done with is more …”
